namibia.overview: Namibia's hiking is defined by dramatic desert landscapes, including the otherworldly red sands of Sossusvlei, where an easy walk reaches the clay pan of Deadvlei with its ghostly skeletal trees, and hikers can tackle the climb up the spine of the 1000-foot Big Daddy Dune for panoramic desert views. Immense Fish River Canyon allows for a demanding 53-mile, multi-day trek. The canyon trek requires a permit and a doctor's certificate, and is strictly limited to the cooler months to avoid extreme heat.

months.2: Intense heat keeps the multi-day canyon route closed. Any walking, such as climbing Big Daddy Dune, must be done right at sunrise before the sand becomes too hot to handle.
months.7: Excellent conditions continue for the Fish River Canyon trek. The cool days allow hikers to safely navigate the gorge floor, while dawn walks up Big Daddy Dune yield spectacular views.
months.8: The prime walking window holds strong. The 53-mile Fish River Canyon trek is fully open, and the cool mornings make the steep sand ascent of Big Daddy Dune highly rewarding.
months.12: The desert is extremely hot, keeping the multi-day canyon route closed. Any walking, such as climbing Big Daddy Dune, must be done right at sunrise.

new-orleans.overview: Walking here means short, flat nature trails and urban parks. Couturie Forest in City Park has a mile-long path under the canopy, and Barataria Preserve in Jean Lafitte National Historical Park has boardwalks and dirt paths through swamp and marsh.

nicaragua.overview: Much of the hiking in Nicaragua is focused on rugged day hikes through the cloud forest that surrounds its many volcanic peaks. The signature route is the steep, muddy climb up Volcán Maderas on Ometepe Island, usually done with a local guide, which rewards hikers with a crater lake and sweeping views of Lake Nicaragua. The best hiking conditions fall between December and April.

nova-scotia.overview: Nova Scotia's best hiking traces the rugged Atlantic coastline and the highlands of Cape Breton. The famous Skyline Trail is a short, dramatic loop above the Gulf of St. Lawrence, where hikers often spot moose and whales from the headland boardwalks. Other day hikes along the Cabot Trail lead through deep river canyons and coastal forests.

north-cascades.overview: The North Cascades are home to some of the most dramatic alpine hiking in the United States, with steep trails leading to jagged peaks, deep valleys, and hanging glaciers. Day hikes like the long, steep climb up Sahale Arm or the shorter Cascade Pass deliver views of a vast, icy wilderness. The season is short, dictated by heavy winter snows that close the main highway for months, making late summer the only reliable window for the high country.

nyc.overview: Walking here means easy nature paths within the five boroughs: the wooded trails of Inwood Hill Park, the Staten Island Greenbelt and the extensive trails through the forests, lawns and gardens of Central Park. All can be reached by subway or ferry and give a break from the dense urban environment.

okinawa.overview: Okinawa holds modest but rewarding hiking, mostly in the subtropical Yanbaru forest in the north and on coastal paths. Trails are short, from easy boardwalks to the muddy old logging road up Yonaha-dake, the island's highest peak, where hikers turn back at the ninth station marker. Winter is best, avoiding summer heat and typhoons.

pakistan.overview: Pakistan's Karakoram range offers dramatic expedition trekking, dominated by the multi-week route up the Baltoro Glacier to K2 Base Camp. Shorter hikes reach the high pastures of Fairy Meadows beneath Nanga Parbat, while the Hunza Valley provides lower-elevation trails. The high-altitude routes require serious commitment, and the K2 trek mandates an approved guide and agency.

palau.overview: Palau is primarily a water destination, but a few short walks exist on the larger islands. The most notable is the brief, steep trail through the jungle to Ngardmau Waterfall on Babeldaob.

panama.overview: Panama's tropical hiking landscapes range from the cloud forests of the western highlands to the lowland rainforests near the canal. The best-known routes center around Boquete, including Sendero Los Quetzales, which climbs through remote cloud forest to link the villages of Cerro Punta and Boquete, and challenging hike up Volcán Barú for views that can stretch to both oceans on a clear day. Trails are often muddy and humid, with the dry season providing the most reliable conditions.

papua-new-guinea.overview: Papua New Guinea is defined by the Kokoda Track, a grueling 60-mile, eight-day trek through dense jungle and steep, muddy ridges, with a permit required. Hikers come for the wartime history and the remote Owen Stanley Range. Beyond Kokoda, the highland valleys have shorter day hikes to remote villages and birding sites. The trails are driest from May to September; heavy rains turn the paths into deep mud for much of the rest of the year.

paris.overview: From Paris, a short train ride reaches the vast Fontainebleau forest and sections of the GR11 loop. Walkers find easy to moderate day hikes through ancient woodlands, sandstone ridges, and quiet countryside. The city itself offers only flat urban park strolls.

peru.overview: Cusco and the Sacred Valley offer some of the most famous trekking on Earth, leading through the high Andes to ancient ruins. The multi-day routes are the main draw, led by the famous four-day Inca Trail to Machu Picchu and the 5-6 day high-altitude Salkantay trek past glacier-capped peaks. Day hikers can tackle the steep, breathless climb to Rainbow Mountain at over 16,000 feet, or explore shorter paths connecting Inca sites above the valley. The best conditions run from April to October, while heavy rains disrupt routes early in the year.

peruvian-amazon.overview: Walking in the Peruvian Amazon means guided excursions from jungle lodges, reached by boat or small plane. Walks are slow, hot, and humid, and focus on the dense rainforest rather than sweeping views. Conditions vary little through the year, though trails are firmer and rivers lower in the drier months.

months.1: Heavy rain keeps the forest floor wet and muddy and rivers run high, so lodges lean on boats and short guided walks on higher ground.
months.2: Rain stays heavy and rivers high. Guided walks stick to higher ground near the lodges, and mud is constant.
months.3: Rain remains frequent and rivers are still high, though some higher ground is walkable and guides mix walks with boat trips.
months.4: Rains begin to ease and trails slowly firm up, allowing slightly longer guided walks, though mud is still a constant.
months.5: Drier weather takes hold and more trails become accessible. The walking is still hot and humid, but the ground is firmer.
months.6: Drier months bring firmer trails and lower rivers, allowing guides to lead longer walks through the dense forest to spot wildlife and reach clay licks.
months.10: Rains begin to return, softening the trails. Walking is still very possible, but expect increasing mud and humidity on guided excursions.
months.11: Rain becomes more frequent and trails grow muddy, so guided walks are shorter and boat trips take a larger share.
months.12: Heavy rains set in and the lower trails turn wet, so walks stay on higher ground near the lodges and the experience is very wet and muddy.

provence.overview: Provence's hiking options range from the steep limestone fjords of the Calanques National Park on the Mediterranean coast to the trails connecting the hilltop villages of the Luberon. Routes range from easy coastal paths to challenging mountain climbs, with the best hiking found in the cooler shoulder seasons.

puerto-rico.overview: Puerto Rico's lush tropical hiking options are anchored by the dense rainforest trails of El Yunque and the steep, forested paths of the Cordillera Central. Hikers navigate muddy tracks to reach hidden waterfalls, observation towers, and sweeping views of the Caribbean coast.
